profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, traded on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue was $215,938,000,000, based on a 10-K filing with a period ending January 25, 2026. The company's site, focused on its AI model offerings, describes NVIDIA as a builder of foundation models and deployment infrastructure for enterprise and developer use.

The company's primary AI model product is NVIDIA Nemotron, which the site describes as a family of multimodal, open AI models designed for agentic AI workflows including reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation, speech recognition, text-to-speech, neural machine translation, and multimodal vision tasks. The site highlights Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as a variant aimed at faster task completion, and NeMo Switchyard as a routing component for directing agent steps to appropriate models. NVIDIA publishes model weights, training datasets, and training techniques under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the site describes as permissive and allowing commercial use and modification without requiring credit to NVIDIA. Nemotron models are available as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which the site describes as optimized inference microservices for enterprise deployment requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, with access and downloads available at build.nvidia.com. Bryan Catanzaro, identified as VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is cited on the site in connection with the vision behind Nemotron.

The held facts record 175 legal cases with California exposure and assign NVIDIA a CIK of 0001045810, confirming its status as an SEC-registered public company. No MCP server registrations or active lawsuit details are recorded in the current data.
